title: Appendix B: Non-Parametric Validation of Scale-Adaptive Interaction Test Results via GAMM and Aligned Rank Transform (ART)
text: Method 1: Generalized Additive Mixed Models (GAMM) ARIMA-Ordered Measurement Structure. Framework: Semi-parametric model combining flexible smooth functions (thin-plate splines) mixed-effects structure; assumes additive model Y = f₁(q) + f₂(condition) + f₃(q, condition) + subject-intercept + ε f terms smooth rather linear. Paired design structure: Uses random intercepts subject (~1|subject) AR(1) correlation structure accommodate repeated entropy measurements across q-values within subject. hierarchical approach preserves paired sample structure modeling autocorrelation q-ordered measurements. Distributional assumption: Uses Gaussian residuals (standard mixed-effects models); automatically detects bounded support [0,1] entropy applies Gaussian family due mgcv::gamm() limitations extended families paired designs. Treatment entropic structure: Treats q-values time-like ordered measurements within subject, applies ARIMA(1,1,0) first-differencing remove monotone trend ensure stationarity; AR(1) correlation structure captured nlme::corAR1() specification. Heteroscedasticity handling: Automatically detects variance heterogeneity (Breusch-Pagan test); however, heteroscedasticity-based variance weights applied paired designs due mgcv::gamm() limitations. Key advantage: Captures smooth nonlinear q × condition interactions accommodating paired sample correlation structure random intercepts AR(1) correlation modeling; includes small-sample bias correction n < 20. Method 2: Aligned Rank Transform (ART) — State---art non-parametric interaction testing, Hochberg Step-Correction. Falls back Conover-Iman Rank Transform via method='rt' needed. Framework: Pure non-parametric method via ARTool package (Kay et al. 2021). Strips main effects ranking (“alignment”) preserve interaction structure (Higgins Tashtoush 1994; Wobbrock et al. 2011). Zero parametric distributional assumptions. Distributional assumption: None; operates entirely aligned ranks. Valid continuous distribution correlation structure. title: TSENAT
text: RNA-seq analysis typically addresses one three complementary biological questions: (1) genes change total abundance?, (2) individual transcripts shift abundance?, (3) transcripts shift proportions within genes, independent total abundance? However, fourth question remains largely invisible: isoform-usage complexity change?

title: TSENAT
text: TSENAT captures isoform-usage complexity throught Tsallis entropy, whose entropic index parameter (q) enables evaluate different data dimensions: Low q (e.g., 0.5): Focuses rare isoforms - detects diversity maintained collapsed Mid q (e.g., 1.0): Balanced view (Shannon entropy) - overall isoform complexity High q (e.g., 2.0): Focuses dominant isoforms - detects dominance shifts examining diversity across multiple entropic indices (q-values), TSENAT allows identify scale-dependent diversity changes - hallmark coordinate isoform switching.

title: TSENAT
text: Tsallis entropy parametric family diversity measures generalizes Shannon entropy enables tuning sensitivity different scales isoform organization. Mathematical Definition: discrete probability vector p=(p1,…,pn)p = (p_1, \ldots, p_n) representing isoform proportions within gene, Tsallis entropy : Sq=1−∑=1npiqq−1S_q = \frac{1 - \sum_{=1}^{n} p_i^q}{q - 1} elegant formula unifies diverse diversity concepts specific entropic indices (q-values): q = 0: Richness — Simple count expressed isoforms; emphasizes rare variants strongly. q = 1: Shannon entropy — Standard information-theoretic measure; balanced weighting across scales. q = 2: Gini-Simpson index — Probability two randomly-drawn transcripts different; robust rare variants.

what: Divergence Analysis: Measuring Information-Theoretic Distance Between Conditions
title: TSENAT
text: Tsallis entropy quantifies diversity within single distribution, Tsallis divergence DqD_q measures information-theoretic distance two distributions. Mathematical Definition (Furuichi formula): two probability distributions PP QQ representing isoform proportions control treatment conditions, Tsallis divergence : Dq(P||Q)=1−∑ipiq⋅qi1−qq−1D_q(P||Q) = \frac{1 - \sum_i p_i^q \cdot q_i^{1-q}}{q-1} pip_i qiq_i probability values position ii. Tsallis divergence enables quantification fundamentally different isoform complexity patterns experimental conditions.

title: Detect q-dependent gene interactions — calculate_rank_transform
text: ## Key Features - **Q\(\times\) Condition Interaction**: Tests entropy patterns across q-values differ   condition (main discovery goal) - **Multi-q Analysis**: Combines diversity results multiple q-values   single SummarizedExperiment joint hypothesis testing - **Aligned Rank Transform (ART)**: State---art non-parametric interaction   testing via ARTool package (default). Strips main effects ranking   preserve interaction structure (Higgins & Tashtoush 1994, Wobbrock et al. 2011). - **Conover-Iman Rank Transform**: Two-way non-parametric ANOVA ranks   (fallback via `method='rt'`) - **Multiple Testing Correction**: Hochberg, Benjamini-Yekutieli, permutation   (Westfall-Young) procedures - **AR(1) Correlation Handling**: Westfall-Young preserves q-value spatial   correlations (important ordered q measurements) - **Effect Sizes**: Eta-squared (\(\eta^2\)) q\(\times\) condition interactions ## Statistical Hypotheses Tests null hypothesis: - H0 = Gene entropy q-effect differ conditions (q-independent) - H1 = Gene entropy q-dependence CONDITION-SPECIFIC (interaction exists) significant interaction indicates condition-specific patterns entropy varies across q-value spectrum, revealing biological processes specific condition. ## Biological Example Gene shows strong isoform switching (q-dependent entropy) tumor cells healthy cells -> Identified disease-relevant q-dependent gene. condition-specific q-dependent genes: - **Condition **: Strong entropy variation across q (q-dependent isoform usage) - **Condition B**: Flat entropy profile across q (uniform isoform usage) - **Interaction**: Condition-specific q-dependence pattern reveals disease-associated   splicing regulation Analyzes gene interactions change across q-value spectrum using rank-based (Conover-Iman Rank Transform) statistical tests. **Parameter resolution priority** (explicit > @config > default/auto-detect): condition_col: REQUIRED - must explicitly provided q: ALWAYS auto-detected diversity_results (q-values tested together) paired: explicit arg > @config$paired > FALSE (default) subject_col: explicit arg > @config$subject_col multicorr:  explicit arg > @config$multicorr > 'hochberg' nthreads: explicit arg > @config$nthreads > 1 (default) nperm_mode:  explicit arg > @config$nperm_mode > 'standard'

Note: Use adequate complexity (transcripts/genes, samples, expression)  # to avoid filtering away all genes during diversity computation n_genes <- 50 n_transcripts_per_gene <- 30 n_transcripts <- n_genes * n_transcripts_per_gene n_samples <- 16  # 8 subjects x 2 conditions (paired design)  # Generate counts with clear biological signal control_idx <- seq(1, n_samples, by = 2) treatment_idx <- seq(2, n_samples, by = 2)  counts <- matrix(0, nrow = n_transcripts, ncol = n_samples) for (j in seq_len(n_samples)) {   lambda <- if (j %in% control_idx) 100 else 180   counts[, j] <- rpois(n_transcripts, lambda = lambda) } counts <- pmax(counts, 50)  # Ensure minimum expression  rownames(counts) <- paste0('TX_', seq_len(n_transcripts)) colnames(counts) <- paste0('Sample_', seq_len(n_samples))  # Create rowData with gene mapping (tx2gene structure) rowdata <- data.frame(   transcript_id = rownames(counts),   gene_id = rep(paste0('GENE_', 1:n_genes),                  each = n_transcripts_per_gene),   row.names = rownames(counts) )  # Compute diversity (prerequisite for SAIT interaction analysis) analysis <- calculate_diversity(   analysis,    q = c(0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5) )  # Calculate q x condition interactions using GAM analysis <- suppressWarnings(calculate_sait(   analysis,   condition_col = 'condition',   method = 'gam' ))  # View top interaction results using unified accessor (first 3 genes) res <- results(analysis, type = "sait") if (!is.null(res)) head(res, 3) } # }

title: TSENAT 0.99.0
text: Initial Bioconductor release. TSENAT provides scale-dependent analysis transcript isoform diversity using Tsallis entropy, enabling detection splicing-driven regulatory changes orthogonal count-based differential expression methods. Core analysis via calculate_diversity(), calculate_divergence(), calculate_rank_transform() Q×Condition interaction testing, calculate_sait() scale-adaptive interaction testing (GAM, LMM, GEE, FPCA) AR(1) support repeated measures, calculate_concordance() method comparison. Supports Conover-Iman Rank Transform tests, permutation tests, jackknife bootstrap. Parameter q tunes Tsallis entropy sensitivity: q < 1 emphasizes rare isoforms, q ≈ 1 recovers Shannon entropy, q > 1 emphasizes dominant isoforms. Unified S4 class TSENATAnalysis integrating SummarizedExperiment, configuration, results, cached plots full subsetting accessor support. Data input: build_analysis() RNA-seq count matrices Salmon quantification (via internal utilities); supports GFF3 annotation files transcript--gene mapping via tx2gene parameter. Quality control: filter_analysis() multi-criteria filtering; jackknife_entropy_outliers_s4() outlier detection. Visualization suite (8 plot types): diversity q-curves, volcano/MA plots, violin/density plots, transcript composition heatmaps, divergence distance matrices, interaction surfaces, concordance plots, multi-gene q-spectrum plots. ggplot2-based publication-ready styling. High-level workflow orchestration via TSENAT() flexible configuration management TSENAT_config(). Performance: Rcpp/RcppArmadillo entropy calculations, BiocParallel support, lazy-loading visualization libraries (~30% faster non-plot workflows). Comprehensive documentation: main vignette + 2 appendices (SplicingFactory validation, advanced workflows), 25 exported functions complete roxygen2 documentation.
